summary: The study investigates the deposition of HfO2 on GeOxNy/Ge gate stacks using atomic layer deposition (ALD) to achieve low interface state density and capacitance scaling. The process involves nitridation of Ge surfaces using a remote plasma source with a H2/N2/Ar gas mixture at temperatures between 300–435 °C. The ALD process uses tetradimethylaminohafnium (TDMAHf) and H2O as precursors at 225 °C. The nitrogen content in the GeOxNy layer significantly affects the crystalline structure of the overlying HfO2 and Ge diffusion into the HfO2 layer. The study also explores the impact of nitridation temperature on the interface state density (Dit) and capacitance equivalent oxide thickness (CET).
